card.name: "have" after "These cases" in warnings
card.fires_on: The word "have" right after a subject like "These cases", "These events" or "Reported cases", in adverse-event warnings that follow a sentence saying something has been reported. Weaker on a comma after a statistic.

modes.label: Have after case subject
modes.description: "have" following "These cases", "These events" or "Reported cases" in post-marketing warnings.

modes.label: Comma after a statistic
modes.description: A comma after a figure and date, just before a source is cited.
modes.example: Measles alone killed more than 150,000 people globally in 2011<<,>> according to WHO.

card.writes: It promotes words like "mostly" and "predominantly", which suggests a qualifier about who or when the cases occurred.
card.plain: It fires on "have" when a warning says that these cases have occurred, where a phrase like "mostly in" often comes next.
